scope: Atomic native admission of independent child reservations; existing single-item admission delegates to the same implementation
contracts: All child reservation rows commit in one SQLite Immediate transaction with distinct owner locks and unique sequential CAS generations
No child authority is returned on conflict, count/byte overflow, generation exhaustion or a failed insertion
All ordered child paths and alias dependencies are recaptured after any coordinator-managed revision change
Aggregate request and resource budgets cover all children; write/read and write/write conflicts across independent children are rejected, while read/read sharing is allowed
Children independently promote or finish; releasing one ordinary child preserves its promoted sibling and durable catalog evidence
Unpromoted children from a process that exits without destructors are reclaimed by native OS owner state
Failed commit drops live handles; a later healthy admission reclaims unreferenced owner files

native.scope: Regression of actual single-operation recovery, overwrite Undo/Redo, reload and detached-window settlement using the shared admission implementation; grouped copy execution is not wired

verification.frontend_scope: No frontend source changed in this checkpoint; the preceding warning/refresh acceptance records frontend behavior and typechecking. The production frontend was rebuilt for the bundle check.

independent_review.verdict: CONFIRMED for independent-child atomic admission; reviewed current source, added rollback/promotion/process-exit tests and passing recovery log
independent_review.limits: Unreferenced lock cleanup is eventual and depends on a later healthy admission. No Nth lock-create IO injection was added; the production post-create commit-failure path and owner unwinding were verified.

limitations: This prerequisite does not implement the full copy-batch executor, immutable exact-target planning, ordered overlapping targets, partial-result ledger, batch cancellation or paste/drop integration
Existing repeated-name and overwrite UI semantics still require an ordered higher-level plan; this independent-child primitive must not silently replace those semantics with rejection
Ordinary Copy inverses still need exact published-object identity; atomic forward admission does not protect later inverse execution against a substituted object
Journal revision detects managed admission/effect changes, not arbitrary external filesystem writes after capture; native version/identity checks remain required
Atomic reservation is not atomic filesystem execution or a power-loss proof
Windows/macOS qualification, startup measurements, artifact retirement/quotas and full architectural review/release acceptance remain incomplete
Native binary contains E2E flags; production frontend assets were rebuilt afterward. No publication attempted.
